title: Take Projects Apart to Develop Delegation Skills
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article addresses leaders who struggle to delegate, particularly those with high standards who fear a drop in quality if they let go of direct control. Its proposed remedy is to break any project or decision into its component sub-tasks — data collection, analysis, option generation, and so on — and start by delegating just one small, defined piece rather than an entire initiative. Leaders are advised to hand off the piece with clear guidelines and success criteria, then genuinely let go. The piece argues that comfort with delegation builds gradually through repeated small wins, ultimately freeing leaders to focus on the strategic work only they can do.
points: Leaders who fear a drop in quality if they delegate can start small by breaking projects into their component sub-tasks.
Delegating just one small, well-defined piece of a project builds comfort and confidence over time.
Clear guidelines, standards, and success criteria should accompany any delegated task — followed by genuinely letting go.
Delegation frees leaders to focus on strategy, decisions, talent selection, and negotiation — work only they can do.
quotes: Fearing standards will drop if they don’t have direct oversight of a project or task, leaders often take the helm even when the best choice would be to delegate.
Delegation is how good leaders leverage their time and focus.
Most projects are made up of dozens of requisite actions and steps. The idea is to get comfortable delegating a small set of them.
Be sure to give those entrusted with the task your guidelines, standards, and insights.
Without the right strategy, does perfect project execution even matter? Learning to delegate isn’t just an imperative. It is a necessity.
